newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rate-related speculation sparked yen rise - Kajiyama.
newsitem.headline: Rate-related speculation sparked yen rise - Kajiyama.

text.p: Speculation in the financial markets about a change in U.S. and Japanese interest rate policies was the cause of the yen's rise on Tuesday, Japan government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told reporters on Tuesday afternoon.
"There is speculation that Japanese rates may rise in the future and that won't happen for the United States," Kajiyama said.
He added, "We must keep in mind, however, that a rapid yen rise will have various effects on industry and such."

Referring to Tuesday morning's announcement that Japanese cabinet ministers held so-called VIP accounts at Nomura Securities Co Ltd, Kajiyama said that investigations would continue into whether politicians' families, employees and political support groups had VIP accounts or received any special treatment from the brokerage.
Kajiyama questioned, however, whether there was a need to single out Nomura's transactions with politicians as a subject for investigation.
Stressing that he was stating a personal opinion, Kajiyama said, "Do we really want to make Nomura in particular the issue?"
He warned that a probe could raise groundless suspicions of illegal activities.
